summary: Tested the new shareable-edit-link feature end-to-end (backend + frontend on the public URL). All 5 backend pytest cases pass (/api/health, POST /api/invites/share, GET .../share/{id}, 404 path, upsert overwrite). On the frontend, after fixing two blockers in /app/frontend/app/editor.tsx the full UX works: the editor renders, all regression testIDs (save-invite-btn, tool-text/background/color/font/layout/ai) are present, the new `share-edit-link-btn` posts to /api/invites/share and a `share-edit-link-url` of the form https://cardcraft-73.preview.emergentagent.com/editor?id=... appears and is copied to clipboard, and visiting /editor?id=agent_test_share_001 in a fresh browser context hydrates the canvas with the stored title 'Hello'. Two coding bugs were fixed by the testing agent to unblock testing (see updated_files / rca_of_issue).

minor.issue: /app/backend/server.py calls `app.include_router(api_router)` twice (once after auth/health routers and again at the bottom). Harmless because FastAPI dedupes routes by path+method, but it is misleading and noisy. Recommend removing the duplicate include.

integration_issues.flow: Get a shareable edit link button
integration_issues.issue: editor.tsx wired the new `share-edit-link-btn` TouchableOpacity to `onPress={onShareLink}` but the `onShareLink` handler was never defined, causing a ReferenceError at module evaluation and a hard crash of the entire /editor route. Testing agent added the missing handler that calls shareInvite(), builds a window.location.origin-based URL, copies it to clipboard, and stores it in `shareUrl` state. Please review and keep.

The remote-fetch fallback in editor.tsx spread the sparse server payload `{title, message, category}` directly into Invite state (`setInvite({ ...(remote.payload as Invite), id })`). This left required fields like `positions`, `background`, `mosaicImages`, `bgFit`, etc. undefined, and InviteCanvas crashed at `invite.positions.title` (src/components/InviteCanvas.tsx:80) with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'title')`. Testing agent fixed by merging the sparse payload with sensible defaults (defaultPositions(), TEMPLATE_IMAGES[cat][0], etc.).

react_native_issues.issue: Console warning: 'shadow*' style props are deprecated. Use boxShadow. (web). Reference: /app/frontend/app/editor.tsx (and possibly other styled components).
Console warning: props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents. Reference: /app/frontend/app/editor.tsx tree.

action_items: Review and keep the new onShareLink handler in /app/frontend/app/editor.tsx (added by testing agent).
Review and keep the merge-with-defaults hydration block in /app/frontend/app/editor.tsx for the params.id remote fetch path.
Address the deprecated `shadow*` style props and `props.pointerEvents` React Native web warnings (minor).
critical_code_review_comments: editor.tsx is 1247 lines — well over the 700-line guideline. Recommend splitting tool panels (text/background/color/font/layout/ai) into separate components.

Leftover/orphan StyleSheet fragment (lines 1199-1233 of the previous file state) caused a Babel SyntaxError and broke the entire web bundle. Testing agent removed the dead block. Suggest CI step to lint editor.tsx (eslint + tsc) before merge.

Sparse server payload + direct spread into typed Invite state is unsafe; consider a typed `hydrateInvite(partial: Partial<Invite>): Invite` helper to keep this logic in one place (the local-storage path on line 84 also assumes the stored record is well-formed).
updated_files: /app/frontend/app/editor.tsx (removed orphan StyleSheet fragment, added missing onShareLink handler, merged sparse remote payload with defaults)
/app/backend/tests/test_share_api.py (new pytest suite for the share endpoints)
seed_data_creation: Created shared invite document {invite_id: 'agent_test_share_001', payload: {title:'Hello', message:'Test', category:'birthday'}} via POST /api/invites/share. Also created TEST_share_upsert_zz used by the upsert test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend share endpoints work and have pytest coverage at /app/backend/tests/test_share_api.py. Frontend share button + cross-browser fetch tested with browser automation. Two coding bugs in editor.tsx were fixed by the testing agent (missing onShareLink handler, sparse-payload hydration crash) — please verify these still exist in the main agent's code review. EditorPage state shape is the source of truth for Invite (see /app/frontend/src/types/invite.ts).
rca_of_issue: Two blockers were introduced with the new feature: (1) /app/frontend/app/editor.tsx had a stray duplicated/orphaned StyleSheet block (lines 1199–1233) that produced `SyntaxError: Missing semicolon` and broke the web bundle (HTTP 500 from Metro). Fix: deleted the orphan block, leaving a single valid `StyleSheet.create({...});` at the end. (2) The new Share button referenced `onShareLink` which was never defined, throwing ReferenceError on render. Fix: implemented the handler. (3) The /editor?id=<share_id> hydration path spread a sparse server payload directly as the Invite, leaving `positions` undefined and crashing InviteCanvas at `invite.positions.title`. Fix: merge payload with defaults (defaultPositions(), TEMPLATE_IMAGES[cat][0], etc.). After all three fixes, both manual share-link generation and cross-browser id-only loading succeed against the public URL.
